1.name: The Porters' Stroll
1.desc: The market's loading crew all went for a walk in the square today, to "have a proper talk about life".
lines: After the walk, the whole crew drops by your place for a rest.

2.name: Afternoon Nap
2.desc: Napping after lunch is all the rage in the neighborhood. All afternoon the street is as quiet as a holiday.
lines: The customers who just woke up are in a lovely mood, though.

3.name: Before You Enter
3.desc: New town rule: before coming in, customers must read a "Dining Preferences Notice" and tick "I agree" item by item. How will you lay it out?
lines: Make a big "Accept all" button
Customers get in fast, then find they've been recommended a pile of dishes they don't want.
List every item honestly
A queue forms at the door, but the inspector praises your compliance.

4.name: The Clock Jumped Ahead
4.desc: Last night the clock tower moved itself forward an hour. Half the town is on the new time, half on the old.
lines: The lunch crowd arrives in two waves.

5.name: The Song Contest Next Door
5.desc: Tonight the TV is showing the next town's song contest. Each costume is wilder than the last, and nobody can explain the scoring. Who are you rooting for?
lines: The twins in tinfoil capes
They won! You cheer at the top of your lungs, and your customers pop the champagne.
They didn't win. You hummed along all night and lost your voice, but you're in a good mood.
The grandpa who sings every song on one note
Grandpa won! You cheer at the top of your lungs, and your customers pop the champagne.
Grandpa didn't win. You hummed along all night and lost your voice, but you're in a good mood.
The electro band with the smoke machine
The band won! You cheer at the top of your lungs, and your customers pop the champagne.
The band didn't win. You hummed along all night and lost your voice, but you're in a good mood.

6.name: Form 27-B
6.desc: A letter from the town hall: the font on your sign isn't in the "Approved Fonts Catalog". Please fill in Form 27-B, attach three supporting documents and get two stamps.
lines: Do it properly
A whole morning of running around. Very educational.
Use the form to prop up a table leg
The table no longer wobbles, but an inspector passing by in the afternoon gives you a long look.

7.name: A Crate of Empties
7.desc: There's a crate of empty bottles in the back alley. The old lady next door says you get a deposit back on every one.
lines: Return them
You get a small handful of coins back.
Give them to the old man who checks the bins every day
He sings your praises to everyone he meets.

8.name: The New Roundabout
8.desc: A new roundabout just opened at the edge of town. Riders go in and can't find the way out, looping round and round.
lines: Deliveries are slower, but all that spinning counts as exercise.

9.name: The Selfie-Stick Tour
9.desc: A tour group waving long sticks squeezes into your restaurant. Every dish gets five minutes of photos before anyone takes a bite.
lines: It's lively in here, but the customers have gotten pickier.

10.name: A Note on the Door
10.desc: The place across the street has a note taped to its door: "Gone to the seaside. See you next month."
lines: Its regulars have no choice but to come to you.

12.name: Fruit in Savory Dishes?
12.desc: Two tables are arguing over whether sweet fruit belongs in a savory dish, and they insist you settle it.
lines: It does
The adventurous eaters stay.
It doesn't
The traditionalists are so pleased they order an extra dish.
Hide in the kitchen
While hiding, you find a voucher under a cupboard.

13.name: The Inspector in a Bow Tie
13.desc: An inspector in a bow tie points at your menu: that sauce may only bear its name if it's made in a certain valley.
lines: Rename it "Something-Style Sauce"
The name got longer, and customers hesitate when ordering.
Invite him to taste a bowl on the spot
He's silent for a long time after eating: "Hmm... perhaps that valley could be a little bigger."

15.name: A Perfectly Straight Queue
15.desc: Somehow, a long, perfectly straight queue has formed outside your door all by itself.
lines: Everyone is very polite. Nobody cuts in, and nobody dares ask what they're actually queuing for.

16.name: The Pot at the Flea Market
16.desc: At the weekend flea market there's a blackened old pot. The seller says it was his great-grandfather's and lets it go cheap.
lines: Buy it
Just an ordinary old pot, but food cooked in it tastes richer.
There's a line of tiny writing on the bottom. You pry it open and find two vouchers tucked inside.
Leave it
You run a hand over the handle, then put it back.

17.name: The Runaway Pig
17.desc: The neighbor's runaway pig spent all morning rooting around your backyard, and dug up a black, very pungent lump.
lines: Return the pig, and the lump, to the neighbor
The neighbor thanks you with a basket of ingredients.
Keep it and experiment
You shave a tiny bit into a dish, and customers keep asking for the recipe.

19.name: Match Night
19.desc: Tonight two towns' teams face off, and everyone is crammed into any place with a TV.
lines: Bring in a TV
Full house, and very loud.
No TV: keep a quiet spot for those who want one
Everyone who comes just wants a peaceful meal.

33.name: Four O'Clock
33.desc: At four sharp, the whole street drops what it's doing for tea and a couple of biscuits.
lines: Tea drinkers pop in on their way.

34.name: Kettles On
34.desc: The moment the evening soap ends, the whole town gets up to boil the kettle, and the power trips with a "click".
lines: You have to relight the stoves, but in that minute of darkness, the customers chat even more.

35.name: The Runaway Cheese
35.desc: Someone rolled a whole wheel of cheese down the hill, and the whole town is chasing after it.
lines: Join the chase
You took a tumble, but everyone had a good laugh.
You caught the cheese first!
Sell hot soup at the bottom of the hill
The worn-out chasers all come for soup.

36.name: Weather Talk
36.desc: Every customer today chats with you about the weather for ten minutes on the way in.
lines: It's slow, but after a good chat nobody's picky.

37.name: Sorry, Sorry
37.desc: A customer stepped on your foot. You both said "sorry" at the same time, then apologized to each other five more times.
lines: The whole restaurant has become extremely polite.

39.name: Bonfire and Fireworks Night
39.desc: On this autumn evening, the town lights a huge bonfire and sets off fireworks. Someone even tossed a scarecrow onto the fire.
lines: Everyone's hungry after the fireworks.

40.name: Quiz Night at the Bar
40.desc: The bar is holding a quiz tonight. Three questions: get them all right and you take home the jar of vouchers on the counter.
lines: Not a single one right. At least you got a free ginger beer.
One right. The bartender gives you a voucher.
Two right. The bartender gives you a voucher.
All correct! The jar of vouchers on the counter is yours.

43.name: No Umbrellas Left
43.desc: Every umbrella in the stand by the door has been borrowed. Customers come in soaking wet.
lines: They ask for hot soup the moment they sit down.

44.name: The Long Neck in the Lake
44.desc: Someone claims to have seen a huge long-necked monster in the lake outside town, but every photo comes out blurry. Tourists flood in.
lines: Go take a look at the lake too
You got a photo! A bit blurry, though.
You got a photo of a floating log.
Stay and look after the tourists
Tourists fill every seat in your restaurant.

49.name: The Ginger Cat's Table
49.desc: A ginger cat has claimed a table for a nap, and nothing will wake it.
lines: Customers line up to pet it.

50.name: The Coin on Its Edge
50.desc: A coin fell off the counter and landed standing on its edge.
lines: You have a feeling today's your lucky day.

51.name: The Heartbroken Head Chef
51.desc: The head chef just got dumped, and every dish is a little too salty today.
lines: But everyone who eats them says: "There's a story in this food."

53.name: Roach Meeting
53.desc: The roaches in the corner seem to be holding a meeting, lined up in a neat row.
lines: All in a row, they're easy to squash.

86.name: The Forgotten Umbrella
86.desc: A customer left their umbrella here yesterday.
lines: Today they came back for it and insisted you take a voucher as thanks.

87.name: A Successful Proposal
87.desc: A customer got down on one knee in your restaurant and proposed. It's a yes!
lines: The whole room applauds, and several tables order more.

96.name: "The Soup Was Too Hot"
96.desc: A bad review appeared online: "The soup was too hot."
lines: Reply politely and promise a warning next time
Someone liked your reply.
Ignore it
A few customers read the review and didn't come in.

100.name: The Customer Without a Wallet
100.desc: A customer finishes eating, pats his pockets, and says he forgot his money.
lines: Let him pay next time
Three days later he came back, with a thank-you gift on top.
You never saw him again.
Have him wash dishes to pay it off
He gets them sparkling.

105.name: The Crooked Sign
105.desc: A gust of wind knocked your sign askew.
lines: Passers-by think it's a new restaurant and come in for a look.

108.name: The Snowman in a Chef's Hat
108.desc: Someone built a snowman outside your door, and it's wearing your chef's hat.
lines: Every customer wants a photo with it.

111.name: The Solo Diner
111.desc: A customer in sunglasses sits alone in the corner, takes one bite of each dish, then jots something in a little notebook.
lines: Treat him specially: two extra dishes on the house
He nods, closes the notebook and leaves.
Treat him like everyone else
He finishes, closes the notebook and leaves.

112.name: A Review in the Paper
112.desc: The Town Daily ran an anonymous food review, and it's about your restaurant.
lines: "Service attentive to the point of suspicion, but the food is genuinely good."

113.name: A Little Plaque
113.desc: Someone mailed you a small brass plaque engraved with a single star. No name.
lines: You hang it by the door.

126.name: Film Crew
126.desc: A film crew borrowed your restaurant to shoot a scene.
lines: Once word got out, the whole town came to watch.

128.name: Meteor Shower
128.desc: There's a meteor shower tonight. You make a wish on the first shooting star.
lines: Early next morning, there are three vouchers in your mailbox.

151.name: A Review in the Paper
151.desc: The Town Daily ran an anonymous food review, and it's about your restaurant.
lines: "A quiet, honest little place."
